7.text: Described from a political cartoon by Victor Gillam in Judge magazine (1899), titled 'A Thing Well Begun Is Half Done.' President McKinley, sleeves rolled up, digs with a shovel at Central America beside a sign reading 'Proposed Nicaragua Canal,' while Uncle Sam carries rifles past the Capitol. American flags fly over the Philippines, Hawaii, Cuba, and Porto Rico. The caption reads: 'Uncle Sam - "Finish the canal, McKinley, and make our national expansion complete in your first administration."'

4.text: Described from Reynolds's Political Map of the United States (1856). The map distinguishes free states and territories (light) from slave states (dark), and shows the territories created under the Kansas-Nebraska Act - Nebraska Territory spanning the northern plains, with an 'Indian Reserve' west of Missouri and Arkansas - visualizing how the Act repealed the Missouri Compromise line.
